claims.claim: If the last day of a legally required period is a holiday, the period extends through the next nonholiday.
claims.quote: If the last day for the performance of any act provided or required by law to be performed within a specified period of time is a holiday, then that period is hereby extended to and including the next day that is not a holiday.

claims.claim: The rule applies to every law requiring an act on a particular day or within a set period.
claims.quote: This section applies to Sections 659, 659a, and 921, and to all other provisions of law providing or requiring an act to be performed on a particular day or within a specified period of time, whether expressed in this or any other code or statute, ordinance, rule, or regulation.

claims.claim: For this rule, all day on Saturdays counts as a holiday.
claims.quote: For purposes of this section, “holiday” means all day on Saturdays

claims.claim: The definition includes all holidays specified in Section 135.
The definition includes Section 12b holidays to the extent that section provides.
claims.quote: to the extent provided in Section 12b, all days that by terms of Section 12b are required to be considered as holidays.

claims.claim: A whole-day closure of a city, county, state or public office counts as a holiday for computing time concerning that office’s business, except for a branch office.
claims.quote: If any city, county, state, or public office, other than a branch office, is closed for the whole of any day, insofar as the business of that office is concerned, that day shall be considered as a holiday for the purposes of computing time under Sections 12 and 12a.
claims.note: The draft retains the whole-day, nonbranch and office-business limits.

claims.claim: Section 135 makes full-day holidays designated by Government Code Section 6700 judicial holidays, subject to listed exceptions.
claims.quote: Every full day designated as a holiday by Section 6700 of the Government Code, including that Thursday of November declared by the President to be Thanksgiving Day, is a judicial holiday, except the date corresponding with the second new moon following the winter solstice, or the third new moon following the winter solstice should an intercalary month intervene, known as “Lunar New Year,”
claims.note: The draft acknowledges the exceptions without claiming to list them.

claims.claim: Government Code Section 6700 lists every Sunday as a holiday.
claims.quote:
(a) The holidays in this state are:
(1) Every Sunday.

claims.claim: Every Saturday is a judicial holiday.
claims.quote: Every Saturday and the day after Thanksgiving Day are judicial holidays.

claims.claim: The day after Thanksgiving Day is a judicial holiday.
claims.quote: Every Saturday and the day after Thanksgiving Day are judicial holidays.

claims.claim: If a judicial holiday falls on Saturday or Sunday, the Judicial Council may choose an alternative observance day.
claims.quote: If a judicial holiday falls on a Saturday or a Sunday, the Judicial Council may designate an alternative day for observance of the holiday.
claims.note: An alternative observance day is discretionary, not automatic.

result.summary: The provided texts in effect on November 19, 2026 support each claim within the stated scope.
